data.name: Bucket
data.Definition: One row of a breakdown: a key, a label, a cost, token counts and a request count. The terminal tables and the model and project charts are drawn from lists of buckets.

data.name: Group by
data.Definition: The choice of breakdown for the terminal summary: model, client, provider, project or day. An unknown name falls back to model.

data.name: Chart colours follow position, not meaning
data.Statement: The picture writer takes colours from one seven colour list by position. In the cost per day chart a colour is a client, in the model chart a rank, and in the token mix chart a token bucket, so the same colour means a different thing in each panel.

refs.quote: color=[PALETTE[i % len(PALETTE)] for i in range(len(buckets))],
ax.barh(labels, values, left=left, label=name, color=PALETTE[index % len(PALETTE)])

data.name: Export writes a chart for a report with no events
data.Risk: The scan command refuses an empty report with a hint and exit code 1, but the export command has no such check, so a png export of an empty report writes a figure with a zero cost title and empty axes and then prints that it wrote the file.
data.Mitigation: Share the empty report check between the two commands, or print a warning before the picture is written.

data.name: Should the four chart colours keep one meaning across panels?
data.Question: Colours are assigned by position in each chart, so a reader can take indigo for a client in one panel and for the top model in another. Checked src/ai_usage_cost/render/png.py. Is a fixed colour per client or per model wanted?
